types/utils.ts/Overwrite: only overwrite keys of objects

Overwrite<string,string> resulted in a mangled object type
because the existing implementation iterated over the string
type's keys (e.g. 'charCodeAt')

This commit changes the implementation so that keys are only
iterated and overwritten in the case of objects. Otherwise,
a non-never TWith type will entirely replace TType, e.g.
Overwrite<string, number> results in 'number'.

summary.intent: Fix inferred procedure input types when middleware follows `.input()`: `Overwrite<string, string>` produced an object of String members, so `Overwrite` now merges keys only when both operands are objects and otherwise lets `TWith` replace `TType`; a regression test is added. No originating issue exists, so issue alignment was unavailable; intent comes from the supplied pull-request text (title, empty template body) and the last commit message.
summary.issue_fit: Partial. The reported string-input-with-middleware case is fixed and the new test type-checks at head but fails at the merge-base. The `any` operand case is not handled and regresses (see finding).
summary.coverage: Both changed files reviewed against the full merge-base diff and the `Overwrite` consumers in `procedureBuilder.ts`, `middleware.ts` and `utils.ts`. Reviewer-executed: `tsc --noEmit` over `packages/tests` at the reviewed head (clean); scratch type probes comparing base and head `Overwrite` and the `any` context trigger; the regression test fails at the merge-base (TS2554 at lines 37-38). The vitest runtime suite was not run, per policy. The forge review threads reference an earlier commit and file name (`issue-5017-...`); the head names it `issue-5020-...`, which the packet does not explain.

findings.title: Keep Overwrite from turning an `any` TType into a union
findings.trigger: `initTRPC.context<any>().create()`, then `t.procedure.use((opts) => opts.next({ ctx: { foo: 1 } })).query(({ ctx }) => ctx.user.id)`.
findings.impact: `any extends object` takes both conditional branches, so `Overwrite<any, {foo: number}>` becomes `{foo: number} | {[x: string]: any}`. `ctx.user` compiles at the merge-base but fails at head with TS2339, a new compile error for any-typed contexts after upgrading.
findings.change: In `Overwrite`, return `TType` when it is `any`: `0 extends 1 & TType ? TType : TType extends object ? ...`. In a scratch copy this makes the trigger and the new regression test type-check.
findings.source: commit-7dc04a7e promises a change only for non-object operands.

findings.title: Drop the unreachable `TType` branch and fix the never doc
findings.trigger: Reading `Overwrite`: `TWith extends any ? TWith : TType` can never take `TType`, and the doc says the whole overwrite happens "unless TWith is never".
findings.impact: For `TWith = never` the result is `never` (probe: `Overwrite<{a: 1}, never>` is `never`), not `TType`, so the doc suggests behavior the type does not have, and the extra conditional layers add nothing.
findings.change: Collapse to `TType extends object ? (TWith extends object ? {...} : TWith) : TWith` and reword the doc to say a `never` TWith yields `never`.

findings.title: Assert on `voidWithMiddleware` or remove it
findings.trigger: The regression test declares `voidWithMiddleware` (no input, middleware, void resolver) but only `str` and `strWithMiddleware` are asserted.
findings.impact: A future change that breaks inference for a no-input procedure with middleware would not fail this test, although the fixture suggests it was meant to.
findings.change: Add expectations on `AppRouterInputs['voidWithMiddleware']` and `AppRouterOutputs['voidWithMiddleware']`, or delete the procedure; the stray `// ^?` markers can go with it.

observations.fact: Arrays and functions still take the key-merge branch because they extend `object`, whereas the runtime input middleware only merges plain objects; the array case is unchanged from the merge-base.
observations.evidence: `packages/server/src/core/middleware.ts:243-249` (`isPlainObject` guard) and the scratch probe result for `Overwrite<{a: 1}, string[]>`, identical at base and head.
